text:
Someone wants to sort the tea in an online shop by price, with a narrow price range.
Sort the tea by price
cheapest tea first, please
Show me tea between ten and twenty-five dollars, lowest at the top
Put the cheap boxes at the top of the list
I'm broke, what's the least I can pay for tea?
Could you please arrange the tea so the lowest prices come first?
Order the teas from small cost to big cost
Hey, line them up from cheap to pricey
I only want to spend twenty-five dollars, so show me the cheapest ones

name: break_reminder
does: Reminds you to take a short break and pick a simple stretch, like swinging each arm, so you don't work too long.
inputs: how many minutes of work before each break, and an optional snack idea, such as something salty or sweet
people say:
- I've been staring at this screen for ages
- Tell me when it's time to rest
- Nudge me every forty-five minutes to stand up
- My shoulders are killing me, make me stretch
- I keep forgetting to take a break

Vesna was packing three school bags at once when her phone buzzed on the kitchen table. She sat down on the comfortable old chair by the window and took a breath. "Excuse me, could you please set a reminder for four o'clock this afternoon? I have to read the new address to the taxi driver for the dance class, and with the children shouting I know I will forget it." The assistant answered, "Done. I will remind you at four o'clock to read the new address to the taxi driver." Vesna asked it to show the address in the note too, and it did. She smiled, zipped the last bag, and went to look for the shoes.

name: post_office_busy_check
does: Checks hourly how busy the post office is, so you know when to go and send a letter.
inputs: which post office, and the day
people say:
- Is the post office packed right now?
- When is the line shortest?
- I need to mail a letter, when should I go?
- Is it worth going before lunch?
- Tell me when it's quiet at the post office on Main Street

name: night_wake_log
does: Records when you wake up in the night, so you do not miss a pattern of frequent wake-ups.
inputs: the time you woke up, and what you ate for dinner, like something with a lot of spice
people say:
- I keep waking up at three
- Why am I up every night?
- Write down that I woke up just now
- How many times did I wake last week?
- I think my late dinner is messing with my sleep

Dmitri was cooking for twenty guests when the kitchen hood started to rattle. The grease filter was full again. It was the third time that month, and the frequent noise was driving him mad. He wiped his hands and spoke to the speaker on the shelf. "Please book a repair man for the hood. I do not want the big expensive service, just somebody to look at the filter." The assistant asked which day was best. "Not Saturday, we are busy. Can you move it to Monday morning?" The assistant booked a visit for Monday at nine and said it would send a note to his phone. Dmitri nodded, turned the burner eye down low, and went back to his soup.

When you order a pizza online, the order goes to the shop, and a driver brings it to your door. A tracker shows where the driver is. People often change small things: the time, the address, or where to leave the box. If the wind could blow the bag away, you might say, 'Leave it inside the gate.' If the driver cannot find your gray house, you can say, 'Ring the bell, it is the second door.' To change the time you can say, 'Make it later,' or 'Can it come sooner?' Most shops let you change things until the food is on its way.

Daniel got home at eight in the morning, tired and in a sour mood. His feet hurt and his head felt heavy. He dropped his bag, sat on the sofa and said, "Call my sister and put her on speaker." The assistant said, "Calling Rosa on speaker now." Rosa picked up. She was at the museum with her kids and had a spare ticket for Sunday. Daniel laughed and said he would sleep first. "Give me a minute," he told her, and then he asked the assistant to turn the volume down and set a reminder for Saturday night. The assistant did both. Daniel closed his eyes.

name: visit_booker
does: Books a visit, such as a class at the library or a haircut, and lets you restart the search with a new day if the time does not work.
inputs: what the visit is for, the day, and the minimum time you need, in minutes
people say:
- Get me in for a haircut on Saturday
- I want a spot at the library story hour
- Is there anything free after work?
- That time won't work, try another day
- Book the dentist for next week

A video is a short moving picture you record with your phone, such as a trip to a camping site on a snowy weekend. People record clips to remember a day or to send to friends. After recording, they often change a few things. They cut the start and the end, make the sound louder, or ask the phone to repair a shaky clip so it looks smoother. To share it they say, 'Send this video to my brother,' or 'Post the clip on the family chat.' If the file is too big, they say, 'Make it smaller.' Most phones can also save the video again with a new name.

A password is a secret word that keeps your accounts private. If you are bored of an old password, or a friend learned it, you can change it. A good password is long and not easy to guess, so rice or 1234 is a poor choice. People ask for changes in simple words: 'Change my password,' 'Make it stronger,' or 'Who can see my photos?' Some phones also lock themselves after a minute. Pay attention to the lock time, and say 'Lock my phone sooner' if you want it faster. Never tell anyone your password, even a person you trust.

A photo album is a place on your phone where pictures are kept together, like a trip or a birthday. People take a picture of a fork on a dinner table or of a big family group, and later they sort the pictures. Common changes are cropping, adding a filter, or making the colors warmer. If a photo looks too orange, you might ask to cool it down. To share, you say 'Send these to Mum' or 'Put them in a new album.' A closed album can only be seen by you, and an open one can be shared with others. If you want a copy of what is on the screen, you say 'Take a screenshot.'

Television is a screen at home that shows channels, shows and films. The remote is what you use to change things. When the red light on the remote starts to blink, the batteries are getting weak. People ask for small changes all the time: 'Turn it up,' 'Switch to channel five,' 'Put on subtitles,' or 'What is on next?' With streaming, you can also say 'Play the next episode' or 'Go back ten seconds.' Some people put on a coat and step outside for a minute, then ask to pause the show. When they return, they say 'Carry on' and the show starts again from the same place.

Every phone has a volume setting that controls how loud the sound is. It is there so you can hear a call in a quiet room or a song in a noisy kitchen. If the dryer is running next door, you may want the sound louder; at night you want it lower. People say 'Turn the volume up,' 'Make it quieter,' or 'Mute it.' Another great setting is do not disturb, which stops calls and alerts for a while. Say 'Do not disturb until seven' and the phone stays silent. Brightness works the same way: 'Make the screen dimmer' is a normal request at bedtime.

A timer helps in many games and puzzles. Say a family plays a board game after dinner while the dishwasher runs. Each turn has a time limit, so no one waits too long. People ask for changes like 'Set a timer for two minutes,' 'Make it longer,' or 'Start again.' Scores are kept too: 'Add five points to Sam' or 'Who is far ahead?' Rules can be changed by the group, and people say 'Let's play with the short rules.' When a puzzle is hard, someone may ask 'Give me a hint' or 'Read the rules again.' When the timer rings, the players come back to the table and count the points.

Someone wants a flat bike route to the grocery store for next Tuesday at noon.
Flat route to the grocery store, next Tuesday at noon
Find me an easy ride to the shops with no hills
I need to cycle to the grocery store next Tuesday around noon, nothing steep
Can you trim the route so it's under five kilometres?
Where can I bike without climbing, Tuesday lunchtime?
My legs are tired, so plan a flat way to the shops for next Tuesday at noon
What's the gentlest cycle path to the grocery store?
Could you please map a level bike ride to the grocery store for next Tuesday at twelve?

name: call_back_later
does: Reminds you to call someone back with a push alert, and marks the contact with a brown dot so you can spot who you missed.
inputs: the contact's name, the time, and a short note, like asking about a vitamin order
people say:
- I missed Jo's call, remind me later
- Ring my mum back at six
- Don't let me forget to call the doctor's office
- Who tried to reach me today?
- Nudge me in an hour to phone Sam

Chiara was stirring pasta with one hand and holding the baby with the other. A school bag by the door had a broken pen sticking out of it. She leaned toward her phone with sticky fingers and typed: "need 3 blue pens delivered befor friday". The assistant understood. It said, "I found a pack of three blue pens and ordered it. It will arrive on Thursday at your address." Chiara sighed with relief. They live on the third floor, and she did not want to carry anything up the stairs after work. She tasted the sauce. It was a little bitter, so she added a pinch of sugar and called the kids to the table.

Person: Quick, put a notice on the street group, my cat Max is lost.
Assistant: I'm sorry to hear that. What colour is Max?
Person: Orange with white paws. No wait, grey with white paws. Sorry!
Assistant: Grey with white paws. Where was he last seen?
Person: Near the cheese shop on Mill Road, about an hour ago.
Assistant: Got it. Should I display your phone number on the notice?
Person: Yes please, that would be perfect.
Assistant: The notice is posted on the street group with your number. I'll tell you if anyone replies.

Aroha stood at the door with her keys in her hand. The morning was chilly, and her ankle was still healing, but the doctor had said short walks were fine. She typed on her phone while hurrying down the stairs: "set a 20 minute wlak timer and count my steps". The assistant understood anyway. It said, "Timer set for twenty minutes. I will count your steps and tell you when the time is up." Aroha pulled her scarf up and went out. When the timer rang she checked the screen: two thousand steps. Not bad for a start, she thought, and she walked home slowly.

name: burn_care_guide
does: Plays out loud the steps for a small burn, including what to avoid, like ice straight from the freezer, and how long an average burn takes to heal.
inputs: where on the body the burn is and how big it is, in plain words
people say:
- I just burned my hand on the stove
- What do I do for a small burn?
- Is it okay to put ice on it?
- My kid touched the oven door
- Is this burn bad enough for a doctor?

Cleaning goes better with a plan. Many homes have a robot vacuum that cleans the floor on its own, and a schedule says when. After you fry fish or eggs, the kitchen gets greasy and needs a quick clean. People change the plan with simple words: 'Clean the kitchen every morning,' 'Skip today,' or 'Do the rough areas twice.' A rough, dirty floor by the door may need more passes. Always put the cap back on the cleaning spray and keep it out of reach of small children. When guests are coming, you can say, 'Start cleaning now,' and if you are on a call, 'Stop, I'm busy.'

Chidi came in from the garden, washed his hands at the faucet and looked at his gloves. "These gloves have more holes than cloth," he said to the speaker on the shelf, and put them on the table. The assistant said, "It sounds like you need a new pair. Here are three strong ones for gardens. The brown pair is the last one in stock." Chidi smiled. "The brown ones, yes. I like to wear something tough." The assistant ordered them, with delivery on Friday, and said it would remind him to check the box. Chidi went back to his tomatoes with his old gloves in his pocket.

A washing machine cleans clothes with water and soap, and a dryer makes them dry with hot air. The dryer gets as hot as a small oven, but you do not want to roast your clothes, so people choose a low heat for soft things. A full machine works better than a half empty one, but too full is bad too. People ask for changes like 'Wash it cold,' 'Make it longer,' or 'Use the quick wash.' When the cycle ends, the machine makes a sound, and some phones can call out 'Your laundry is done.' If there is a stain, you can say 'Soak it first.' Then you fold, or ask 'Remind me to take the clothes out in twenty minutes.'

Thiago, a grandfather of five, was packing for a weekend with his grandchildren in the hills. His tent was already in the car, and he had just heated soup in the microwave for the trip. The sky looked grey. He picked up his phone and said, "Rain tomorrow?" The assistant said, "Yes, light rain in the hills from ten in the morning to four in the afternoon." Thiago nodded. "Pack list," he said. The assistant read out a list: rain jackets, a tarp, dry socks, and a permanent marker to write names on the bags. Thiago laughed. He always forgot the marker.

The power went out while Wei was doing his homework. The house was dark and his mother was still at work. He took a breath and spoke to the tablet. "Turn on the light." The assistant said the light would not work because of the power cut. "Then turn on the flashlight," said Wei. "No, wait, not the light, the one on the tablet." The assistant switched on the tablet flashlight. Wei asked it to name a radio station with news about the power cut, and the assistant named one. He listened. The station said power would be back in an hour. A candle was left on the shelf, but Wei did not touch it. He waited with the flashlight.

Person: Remind me to pay the tax bill.
Assistant: Sure. When should I remind you?
Person: Half an hour before my shift tomorrow.
Assistant: What time does your shift start?
Person: Seven in the evening.
Assistant: Okay, a reminder at six thirty tomorrow. Should I sync it with your calendar too?
Person: Yes, but just a plain reminder, no loud alarm. I'm trying to sleep.
Assistant: A quiet, plain reminder for six thirty, and it's in your calendar now.

name: spending_check
does: Shows how much you spent on one kind of thing this month, such as eating out or what you need to cook at home, and sends a quiet note when you reach your limit.
inputs: the kind of spending, the month, and an optional limit
people say:
- How much did I blow on takeaway?
- Am I over budget on groceries?
- Tell me when I've spent two hundred on food
- Where is all my money going?
- What did I spend last week on coffee?

Person: It's very dark behind the shop at night and it feels creepy.
Assistant: Would you like me to turn on the back light, or switch on the camera there?
Person: The light, I think. Our market tent is out there too and I don't want anyone near it.
Assistant: How long should the light stay on? The minimum I can set is ten minutes.
Person: Until I finish locking up, so about twenty minutes.
Assistant: Done. The back light is on for twenty minutes. I can't lock the tent for you, but I can send an alert if the motion sensor sees someone.
Person: Yes please, do that.

Oscar had just moved to the city and had never ordered anything online before. A woman next door had told him the post was slow here. He asked his phone, "Where is my order, and is it later than they said?" The assistant said the parcel was at the local depot, one day later than planned because of icy roads. Oscar touched the screen to open the map. "Will it come sooner if I pay double for fast delivery?" he asked. The assistant said no, the roads were the problem, not the service, and offered to tell him when it was out for delivery. Oscar said yes and put the kettle on.

Diego ran a small shop, and his young daughter Lia had a school play at the theater on Friday. He wanted to help her practice after closing. He asked the speaker behind the counter, "Homework schedule." The assistant asked, "Do you want to see this week's schedule for Lia?" Diego said yes. It listed spelling on Monday, a map project on Wednesday and the play on Friday evening. "Schedule play practice, Thursday at seven," said Diego. The assistant put it on the family calendar and set a reminder for six thirty. Diego went back to the till with a smile.

Wolfgang stood in the garden with a bag of bean seeds and his daughter. They wanted to plant them at half past six, before supper. His phone buzzed with an urgent message from his mother in Sydney. He asked the assistant, "What time is it in Sydney right now?" The assistant said it was half past two in the morning there. "Then she is awake very early," he said. "Read me her message." The assistant read it out: she needed his sister's phone number. Wolfgang asked the assistant to send it, and then to remind him at half past six about the beans. His daughter was already digging the first hole.

Ananya was not good with her new coffee machine. She pressed three buttons and the machine beeped at her. She asked it, "Make me a strong coffee." The assistant started a strong coffee. Then she remembered her doctor had asked her to drink less. "Wait, I mean medium, not strong. And please keep it low on the milk." The assistant stopped, changed the setting to medium and made the cup with a little milk. Ananya tied her scarf, put the cup on the table to rest for a minute, and thanked the assistant. It was not so hard after all.

A flight is a trip by plane, and each one has a time, a gate and a number. Boards at the airport show departures, and they say if a flight is on time or delayed. The airport can be cold, so people carry a jacket. If the signs are in another language, a phone can translate them. A tidy plan helps: arrive two hours early, find the gate, and wait. People ask in simple words: 'When does my flight leave?', 'Is it late?' or 'Which gate?' If the gate changes, you say 'Tell me where to go now.' If it is delayed, you might say 'Move my pickup to later.'

Someone wants a reminder every hour to stand up while they crack on with a long to-do list.
Remind me every hour to stand up
Hourly stretch alert, please
Ping me twice as often as yesterday, I sat too long
Tell me to move around each hour
My back hurts from sitting, nudge me every sixty minutes
Could you please set a reminder to get up at the top of every hour?
Make me take a break more often
Don't let me sit for more than an hour

Sven was lying on the sofa, bored and cold, with his phone on his chest. He remembered he had to ship Gran's birthday parcel, and he typed to the assistant, "Could you please add ship Gran's parcel to my to-do list and put it at the top? I would like to do it first thing, because the post office closes at noon on Saturday." The assistant put 'Ship Gran's parcel' at the top of the list and said it would remind him at nine. Sven pulled a blanket over his legs. At least now he would not forget. He finished his cold pizza and fell asleep.

Someone wants more films like the cooking movie they just watched.
More like this
Similar films
Find me more
Anything else about cooks?
I really dig that one, what else is like it?
Got any other food movies?
That was great, show me another
Please suggest more films like the one I just finished

Navigation helps you get from one place to another. The phone shows a map, a blue line, and the time the trip will take. If a street is blocked, the map finds a nice quiet way around. People change the route with words like 'Avoid the highway,' 'Take the shortest way,' or 'How long will it take?' If you wipe your wet fingers on your shirt and tap the screen, you can also just say it aloud: 'Go home' or 'Find a petrol station.' People also say 'Find a place for lunch on the way' when they are hungry for a plate of hot food. Traffic changes the time, so the answer is not always the same.

Keoni was closing his shop when he found a drawer full of old bottles and tins behind the counter. Once he had put plastic in the glass bin, a silly mistake, and he did not want to do it again. He asked the assistant, "When is the glass bin collected? The day after tomorrow?" The assistant said yes, glass is collected the day after tomorrow in the morning, and plastic on Thursday. Keoni asked it to remind him tonight to put the bin out. He let his hot tea cool on the counter, sorted the bottles into two bags, and switched off the lights.

Someone wants their favorite website read out loud.
Read this page aloud
Can you read my favorite website to me?
I can't see the screen, say what's on it
Check the news site and read it out
Please read the page slowly, around a hundred and twenty words a minute
Speak the text on this website
My eyes are tired, tell me what the page says
Turn this site into audio

Someone wants to find a movie to watch tonight.
What's on tonight?
I'm bored, there's nothing to watch
I just got back from a jog and want something easy to watch
I'll bake for an hour, so find me a film to put on
Any good film with a thin plot? I'm too tired to think
It's a quiet night in here, shall we watch something?
Find a movie for tonight, please
The kids are asleep and the couch is free

Avi was driving the kids to school when his phone lit up with a voicemail. He asked, "Play the voicemail from my favourite bakery." The assistant played it. The bakery was offering a discount of fifteen percent on Saturday morning. Avi said, "Take a note: bakery, fifteen percent, Saturday." The assistant saved the note and asked if he wanted a reminder on Friday night. "Yes, please," said Avi. In the back seat the children cheered, because Saturday meant warm bread with jam. Avi smiled and turned into the school street.

Person: My knees are telling me something about tomorrow.
Assistant: Would you like the forecast for tomorrow? Which town should I check?
Person: Bristol. I'm walking to the front of the park with my grandchildren.
Assistant: Tomorrow in Bristol: cloud in the morning and rain from two o'clock, about eleven degrees.
Person: Then my knees were right. Can you make the screen blink when rain starts?
Assistant: I can't make the screen blink, but I can send you an alert when rain is close.
Person: That's fine. Will you remind me to take my umbrella and keys?
Assistant: Yes, I'll remind you at nine in the morning.

Someone wants the music on the speaker turned down.
Turn it down
It's way too loud in here
My head hurts from this noise
Total quiet, please
Shift the volume down a few notches
This room is a messy racket, calm it down
The baby is sleeping, and it's loud
Could you please lower the sound a little?

name: pet_door_schedule
does: Opens or locks the pet door at set times, ignores false alarms like a bee buzzing near the sensor, and lets you draw up a weekly plan.
inputs: which door, the times to open and lock, and which pet
people say:
- Let the cat out at seven
- Lock the flap at night
- Don't let strays in
- Can Milo go out now?
- Keep the dog inside while it rains

Ruta had worked all night at the hospital. Now she sat at her sister's table with heavy eyelids. The family was playing a card game, everyone was shouting, and nobody could tell who was winning. She tossed a towel on the sofa and said to the speaker, "It's so loud in here I can't tell who's ahead." The assistant understood and said, "I can calculate the scores. Tell me the points." Ruta read them out: Ruta forty, Jon fifty-five, Mara sixty-two. The assistant said, "Mara is winning by seven points." The room cheered, and Ruta finally went home to bed.

Person: wher is my car, running late for the doctor
Assistant: Which car? You have two saved: the blue van and the pink hatchback.
Person: the pink one
Assistant: The pink hatchback is parked on Elm Street, about two minutes from you.
Person: ok. can you warm it up too, i need to pour my coffee first
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't start the pink hatchback from here. I can set a timer for your coffee, though.
Person: no thanks, just show the way to elm street

The router is a small box that gives your home internet. Everything in your house connects to it by wifi, and each wifi has a name and a password. When guests come for the weekend, many people give them a separate guest password, so the main one stays secret. If the signal is low upstairs, you can move the router or buy a booster. When things go slow, people say 'Restart the router' or 'Why is the internet so slow?' To change the password you say 'Make a new wifi password.' To let a friend join you say 'Share the wifi with Ana.' Then the page loads and things go on as usual.

Person: Can I order two pizzas for my birthday?
Assistant: Happy birthday! Which pizzas would you like?
Person: Cheese. Twice as many as last year, we have a lot of friends coming.
Assistant: I can't place an order for a child by myself. May I ask a grown-up to say yes?
Person: My mum is here. Mum, pull up your phone!
Assistant: I'll show the order to your mum so she can confirm. One order can have a maximum of four pizzas.
Person: Four is fine!

A text message is a short note you send from your phone. Groups of people can talk in a group chat, and a reply goes back to one person or to all. When you are away from home, texts are a way to say 'I am late' or 'Call me later.' People change small things: they make the letters bigger, turn off a chat that is too noisy, or boost the volume of the alert. They say 'Read my last message,' 'Reply that I am on my way,' or 'Tell Mum the wind is bad here and the bus is slow.' A voice assistant can write a text as you speak and send it when you say 'Send.'
